title.title: Kobayashi's canonical ampleness conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: every compact Kähler manifold with no entire curves $\mathbb{C} \to X$ has ample canonical bundle

plain: A shape with no room for an infinite straight-line path must be curved 'outward' in a precise sense

beats.text: What the proof rests on, bottom up
Four of its inputs are other unrefereed results from the same release
No curvature hypothesis at all, unlike every earlier result

steps: No entire curves means derivatives of maps are uniformly bounded
Feed those bounds into the release's minimal-model results
Out comes positivity: the canonical bundle is ample

achievement.label: Kobayashi's conjecture (1970)
achievement.context: Before: only with a curvature hypothesis (Wu–Yau 2016, Tosatti–Yang, Diverio–Trapani)
achievement.note: Downstream of the least-checked parts of the release

voice.text: With no entire curves inside, a compact Kähler manifold should have ample canonical bundle.
Brody's derivative bounds feed into the release's own minimal model results, giving ampleness.
Claimed: true, with no curvature hypothesis at all.

sources.quote: Wu–Yau (Invent. Math. 2016, negative holomorphic sectional curvature)

Uses two other release results as inputs: Fujita freeness (038, Corollary 6.3) and the semialgebraic-universal-cover theorem (058), which itself uses the release's log abundance (034_3) and abelianity (057)
That puts it downstream of the least-checked parts of the release.
I graded what each family claims, not whether it is right.
